chunks: We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim bin Hashim, from his father, from Muhammad bin Sinan, from Mufaddal bin Umar, that he said: I was told by Thabit al-Thumali, from the Master of Worshippers, Ali bin Hussain (peace be upon them both), that he said:

There is not, between Allah and His Proof, a veil, and so, there is not for Allah any cover before His Proof. We are the Gates of Allah, and we are the Straight Path, and we are the Bag of His Knowledge, and we are the Interpreters of His Revelation, and we are the Pillars of His Oneness, and we are the Place of His Secret.

key_terms.حُجَّة: Proof of God (often referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the theological significance of the Ahl al-Bayt as the 'Gates of Allah' and 'Straight Path' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) articulates the Shia doctrine of *al-Wilayah* by identifying the Ahl al-Bayt as the essential mediators (*hujjah*) through whom divine knowledge and guidance reach humanity. This narration underscores their ontological status not merely as scholars, but as the living embodiment of the Straight Path and the 'Gates of Allah,' a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegesis of Quranic verses such as Surah Al-Isra. It highlights their role as the exclusive repository of esoteric truth (*khazinat 'ilmihi*) and the interpreters of revelation, establishing them as the indispensable link between the Creator and the created.
